outcome: No change found since 26 January 2024. The conjecture remains open for n≥5; the pre-2024 partial results (2-rearrangeability, verification for n≤4, Lubiw's shortest-path counterexample and its strengthening) are unchanged, and no new paper resolving a case of the stated problem was found.
summary: Szymanski's conjecture (every permutation on the n-dimensional doubly-directed hypercube can be routed with edge-disjoint paths) shows no change since the frozen revision. I read the current Wikipedia article, which still lists it as unsolved: verified computationally for n≤4, open for n≥5, with the known pre-2024 partial results (2-rearrangeability; Lubiw's dimension-5 counterexample to 1-realizability by shortest paths, and its later strengthening showing hypercubes are not n^(1/2-δ)-realizable by shortest paths for any δ>0). Multiple web searches for post-January-2024 activity — general searches on the conjecture's name, on hypercube permutation routing, on arXiv listings, and specifically checking the paper the triage pass flagged (Chakrabarty–Seshadhri, arXiv:2409.02206, 'Directed Hypercube Routing, a Generalized Lehman-Ron Theorem, and Monotonicity Testing') — turned up nothing relevant. I fetched that paper's abstract directly: it concerns vertex-disjoint path collections between comparable sub-level sets of the directed hypercube for monotonicity testing, and does not mention Szymanski's conjecture or general permutation routing; it is a related-but-different problem (§3.1, a variant, not a case). No AI-related search turned up any connection between an AI system and this specific conjecture — one search surfaced general AI-and-mathematics stories (Jacobian conjecture, Erdős problems, unit distance conjecture) but none referenced Szymanski's conjecture. I agree with the triage's 'none' verdict; this is a genuine, well-evidenced 'nothing happened' case.
competing_reading: None. The scope of the stated conjecture (general permutation routing by edge-disjoint paths on the doubly-directed hypercube) is unambiguous, and the one paper found in the area (arXiv:2409.02206) is clearly about a different question (vertex-disjoint paths between sub-level sets for monotonicity testing, not permutation routing), so there is no genuine ambiguity to flag.
what_would_settle_it: A paper proving or disproving the conjecture for some n≥5 (even a single new case), or extending the computational verification beyond n=4, or a proof/disproof of the general statement, would change the status. None was found.
